subject.title: Allow before_agent_start hooks to override prompt

question: Should OpenClaw add a user-prompt replacement contract for plugins, and should that contract live on before_prompt_build with legacy before_agent_start compatibility or on broader llm_input interception?
rationale: This is a new plugin API that lets enabled plugins rewrite model-bound user input, so automation should not choose the trust boundary, hook precedence, or audit behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add prompt-build replacement
options.body: Add a documented replacement field to before_prompt_build, carry it through legacy before_agent_start compatibility, enforce allowPromptInjection filtering, and cover embedded, CLI, and harness runners.

options.title: Use broader LLM interception
options.body: Defer this issue to an llm_input-style modifying hook if maintainers want prompt rewriting at the provider-boundary rather than the prompt-build boundary.

options.title: Reject prompt replacement
options.body: Keep plugin prompt hooks additive-only and direct oversized-prompt mitigation to context-engine or provider-side limits instead.

recommendation.title: Add prompt-build replacement
recommendation.body: Add a documented replacement field to before_prompt_build, carry it through legacy before_agent_start compatibility, enforce allowPromptInjection filtering, and cover embedded, CLI, and harness runners.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent history on shared prompt hook parity and Codex harness prompt behavior, which are central to the cross-runner decision.
